proposedchanges.title: PBS and PolitiFact Compared Trump’s Promise Claim With the MAGA-Meter
proposedchanges.description_short: PBS and PolitiFact Compared Trump’s Promise Claim With the MAGA-Meter
proposedchanges.description_long: In a March 4, 2026, PBS NewsHour report, Trump’s claim that he had kept all his campaign promises was compared with PolitiFact’s MAGA-Meter. The public tracker listed 75 second-term promises and marked about 19 percent as kept at the time. Readers could compare the broad statement with the status assigned to each commitment. PBS cited fulfilled examples that included pardons for January 6 defendants and an extension of the 2017 tax cuts. PolitiFact’s measure assessed whether a stated pledge had been completed, not whether readers should support the policy or whether it was beneficial. Its categories and selected list provide a reference for evaluating the claim, but the figure applies only to those 75 promises and to the date of the report. It is not an exhaustive count of every campaign promise or a final assessment of the term. The comparison makes Trump’s broad claim testable against a recorded set of statuses while leaving policy judgments to readers.

evidencebasis: The packet and latest descriptions identify a PBS report comparing Trump’s claim with a dated PolitiFact tracker of 75 promises, about 19 percent marked kept. The PBS URL remains in source_urls.
notes: The medium already explains the comparison and clarifies what its status labels do and do not measure.
